verdict.rationale: Superpowers documents single-command installs that are active at session start. Devin CLI uses `devin plugins install obra/superpowers`, and skills auto-trigger at session start. Claude Code uses in-agent `/plugin marketplace add` plus `/plugin install`. On Antigravity the session-start hook makes it active from the first message. A real runtime probe confirmed `npx skills add obra/superpowers` fetches and installs skills cleanly. Missing for 10: hands-on verification that skills activate in the next session, a uniform one-liner across harnesses (install differs per harness; Codex/OpenCode use a fetch-and-follow INSTALL.md and Hermes uses a git clone), and Claude Code's marketplace flow being two commands rather than one.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install a skill collection with one documented command — a package-manager one-liner, CLI, or in-agent marketplace command — and it is active in my next session

citations.quote: `devin plugins install obra/superpowers` now works, and skills auto-trigger at session start.
Antigravity runs the plugin's session-start hook, so Superpowers is active from the first message. Reinstall with the same command to update.

a REAL end-to-end keyless install into a scratch project dir — `npx -y skills add obra/superpowers --skill test-driven-development -a claude-code -y --copy` fetched the repo, copied the skill to ./.claude/skills/test-driven-development/
